title: Quick Play: server-run public rooms
summary: Quick Play is a new top row on the main menu. Pick Race or Stunts and the game server puts you in a room that runs itself: lobby, map vote, countdown, race, podium, then Rematch or the next vote.
details: Lobby lasts up to 20 s and starts early when the room is full or everyone presses GO. CPUs fill a race to 6 riders, at most 4 CPUs.
Vote: three mixed-mode cards plus Random, 12 s, weighted roulette. Podium: 8 s, Rematch is the default.

The server checks race results (monotonic laps, speed cap, time floor, drift from GO of 3% or less). A refused result ranks DNF; verified results are written to a match record with the rider's player id.

Touch, keyboard and controller all work; the panel fits 360 px portrait. Protocol adds RoomLoop and Vote packets; older clients are unchanged. Note: research/QUICK_PLAY.md. PR #663, part of the modern multiplayer epic #631.

Verification: unit tests for the server loop and panel; browser test tools/test_engine_quickplay.mjs passed on CI build 43650337246 (menu, tiles, queue, phone joins the same room, GO, vote, driver-started CPU race, checked podium, rematch). Host-only evidence: browser tests on host Chromium against a local game server. Nothing was checked on physical phones.
limitation: A rider drives each round (the server owns the loop, vote, podium and records, but CPU physics and game rules still run on a rider's machine). A room seats 4 humans plus up to 4 CPUs, so a lone racer gets a field of five. CPU difficulty is fixed at Normal. The speed cap and drift allowance are guesses, so a very laggy rider could be refused. The later podium overlap/colour fix was not browser-verified when #663 merged.
caption: Quick Play vote: three map cards plus Random, rider seats with CPU tags and ping bars
